sm: The speaker, Andrew Sandlin, riffs on the novel A Confederacy of Dunces to criticize what he calls principled anti-intellectualism among some young Christian men. He cites an article describing young men who are tired of scholarship and want a heroic masculinity built around being physically ripped and looks maxing, an idea he links to the pagan outlook in the book Bronze Age Mindset. He says physical fitness is part of masculinity but a very narrow part, and he objects to abandoning reading, study and the life of the mind, noting the obsession with memes and mockery, the inability to follow a long argument, plagiarism, and avoidance of hard scholarship. He does not say every young man must be a scholar, and points to autodidacts like A. W. Tozer, Martyn Lloyd-Jones and Charles Spurgeon as serious readers. He calls for young men to pursue both physical and mental fitness by reading books and long essays, studying opponents' views, using logic and avoiding personal attacks. He blames part of the problem on few young men entering mostly secular universities while many young women come out as feminists, and says the Christian faith has always valued the intellect, citing Moses, Paul and Solomon. He closes by urging anyone in this group to repent and become a student of scripture and good literature, and mentions a December fifth symposium addressing both artificial intelligence and anti-intellectualism.
